subject: Flexible true-up + price-cap offer for 2027 renewal
messages:
From: Anna Ruiz <anna@cobaltdesigns.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options — need to lock pricing without losing flexibility

Ben —

Thanks for the heads up about rate movements for 2027. Our CFO is asking for a path to avoid a >15% per-token increase at renewal, but we also need to keep the ability to scale up/down without large stranded spend.

What options do you have for:
- locking a price across the next 2–3 years, and
- allowing us to start at a conservative usage level and ramp with credits/true-ups?

We prefer an approach that limits upfront commitment but still gives a tangible price cap if we choose to grow. Can you share a pragmatic structure and an example P&L impact?

Thanks,
Anna
VP, Platform Engineering
Cobalt Designs

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Ruiz <anna@cobaltdesigns.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cobaltdesigns.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal options — need to lock pricing without losing flexibility

Anna — thanks for outlining the constraint. Below is a concise option that a few customers have adopted when they want pricing certainty without a heavy upfront lock. I attached a one-page term sheet and a sample ramp schedule (spreadsheet).

Summary (high level):
- 3-year price-cap agreement: we lock the per-token price at current 2026 list minus 18% for the length of the agreement.
- Phased prepay/ramp credits: customer prepays the equivalent of 30% of expected 1st-year consumption up front, then replenishes via scheduled tranche payments at the start of year 2 (20%) and year 3 (10%).
- True-up and credit mechanism: if actual usage in year N exceeds the prepay tranche for that year, we true-up at the agreed capped rate. If usage is below the tranche, unused credit carries forward for up to 12 months.
- Safety net / escape: 60-day exit window after year 1 with a modest unwind fee (3% of remaining credit) to preserve flexibility.

Example (100M tokens annual baseline):
- Year 1 prepays 30M tokens at capped price (credit applied as used).
- Year 2 prepays 20M tokens; customer true-ups if they exceed combined credits.
- Effective blended discount across 3 years: ~15–18% vs list, depending on final ramp.

Pros/cons:
- Pros: price certainty, no wholesale stranded spend (credits roll forward 12 months), predictable runway for capacity planning.
- Cons: requires staged cash outflow; larger discounts tied to multi-year commitment.

I attached a clean term sheet (RW-COB-v3-term-sheet.pdf) and a sample ramp workbook (RW-COB-3yr-ramp.xlsx). If this looks reasonable, we can draft a short paperwork bundle (commercial + standard SOW) and run it through finance/legal.

Would you like us to model three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) against your FY27 budget? Happy to set a 30-minute call this week.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: RW-COB-v3-term-sheet.pdf, RW-COB-3yr-ramp.xlsx)

Anna —

Thanks for the quick response earlier. We took your ask and tightened the commercial into a single-play option that should meet Cobalt's objectives: price certainty with staged cash flow and limited stranded risk. Key updates from the internal review are inline below and reflected in the attached updated term sheet (RW-COB-v3-term-sheet.pdf):

Key commercial points (final):
- 3-year price cap: locked at current list minus 18% for the term.
- Prepay tranches: Year 1 = 30% of baseline (due on signature); Year 2 = 20% (due start Y2); Year 3 = 10% (due start Y3).
- Credit carry-forward: unused credit carries forward up to 12 months and is capped at 25% of the receiving year's tranche.
- True-up: overages billed at capped rate at year-end; under-usage credit applies to the following 12 months only.
- Exit: 60-day exit after year 1 with a 3% fee on remaining credit balance.

Next steps:
1) If this works, I will send a DocuSign bundle (commercial + SOW) and an ASC-friendly amortization schedule for your finance team.
2) If you want a more conservative cash profile, we can model alternative tranche mixes (e.g., 20/20/20) — happy to run a scenario.

I attached the term sheet and the ramp workbook. Let me know if you'd like to schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk the numbers with Monica looped in.
